newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 9.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 9.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Monday:
* On Friday, the Dow Jones industrial average surged 130.49 points to close at 7,435.78 as Wall Street took the government's May employment report as a sign that interest rates will not move higher.

* Indonesia's President Suharto celebrated his 76th birthday quietly at his residence in Jakarta on Sunday. Contrary to what has become a tradition in the past, the president this year did not celebrate his birthday with close relatives.

* State Minister of Investment Sanyoto Sastrowardoyo said that total foreign investment applications were down 36 percent in the first five months in 1997 compared with the same 1996 period due to the general election.
* On Friday, the Jakarta Composite Index rose 3.03 points to close at 695.02 after hitting an intra-day high of 696.15 points.
* On Monday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,429.50/30.50 at 0145 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,429.00/30.00.

* Blue chip Bank Negara Indonesia on a report in Bisnis Indonesia saying that the government will merge the current seven state-owned banks to become four banks : Bank Negara Indonesia, Bank Export Import, Bank Dagang Negara and Bank Rakyat Indonesia. The reports could also affect sentiment on other banking stocks.
* Bank Mashill following reports that Bank Brussels Lambert of Belgium has bought a 10 percent stake from its outstanding shares in the market.

* Electricity transformer producer PT Trafindo Perkasa on a report in Bisnis Indonesia that it will become a holding company by acquiring an 80 percent stake in privately-owned telecommunications firm PT Telekomindo Prima Karsa.

* Telecommunications firms PT Telkom Indonesia and PT Indonesia Satellite on an announcement by the ministry of Post, Tourism and Telecommunication that Indonesia will allow new mobile telecommunications services.

* Travel and tourism company Bayu Buana on a report that the company was negotiating to buy franchise rights from a United States-based entertainment company. The company had indicated its first quarter net profit rose 102 percent from the same 1996 period and is expected to book a net profit of 13.5 billion rupiah for 1997.
* Ciputra Development after its subsidiary Ciputra Adigraha Finance BV secured a syndicated loan of US$260 million to support its property projects.
* Property firm PT Jakarta International Hotels and Development on its plan to issue 600 billion rupiah five-years bonds.
